model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (frozen base, no adapter), vision tower Qwen3_5VisionModel
data: 160 experimental images, 10 identities, held-out protocol: train-split exemplars/prototypes -> test queries

mean_pooled_merger_tokens.note: DEGENERATE: all images collapse to one direction; mean-pooling post-merger tokens erases identity signal. Identity information is not in the mean component of the token stream fed to the LM.

pooler_output.note: PERFECT separation (30/30 test images) but extremely tight geometry: identity direction is a tiny subspace component riding on a near-constant shared embedding.

interpretation: The frozen visual stack separates all 10 synthetic identities perfectly (1-NN = prototype = 1.0 on held-out test images), while I2N under language-attention-only LoRA is ~0.13.
Therefore the failure is NOT face discriminability / representation quality (Case B is excluded). It is specifically the visual->textual alias binding / readout path.

Caveat that sharpens the mechanism: the identity signal is real but minuscule in cosine terms (gap 0.0147; between-identity cosine 0.976). A rank-8 LoRA restricted to language self-attention must amplify this tiny component through frozen cross-modal fusion; this is plausible for 2 identities (calibration I2N=1.0) but collapses under 10-way interference.

The degenerate mean-pool additionally shows the identity signal is carried in non-mean (structured) components of the merger token stream, which frozen fusion does not expose prominently to language-side adaptation.
recommended_next_step: Widen trainable scope to the cross-modal path: LoRA (or full fine-tune) on the vision merger / multimodal projector / cross-attention, so the tiny identity component can be amplified before language readout. The capacity-curve sweep (GPU 2) will quantify the N-dependence of the interference collapse.
